teaser.text: SEGRO is a property company that owns, develops and manages industrial buildings. A pound comes in mainly as rent, then goes out on property costs, staff, financing, investment and shareholder distributions.

stock.title: SEGRO stock forecast
stock.meta_description: SEGRO's weighted forecast is broadly flat, with rent capture and development delivery deciding the outcome.
stock.opening: SEGRO's weighted price is 895.28p in October 2029. The investment turns on whether rent capture and development delivery beat vacancy, funding and property-yield pressure.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how SEGRO's business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the outcome.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for SEGRO's forecast?

paragraphs.text: The bear path falls to £515 million and then £488 million before reaching £474 million. It assumes weaker leasing, delayed projects and higher finance costs. Vacancy reached 5.5% in H1 2026, and only 58% of first-half completed space was leased. The bull path reaches £569 million, then £610 million and finally £651 million, requiring stronger occupancy and faster development leasing. Data-centre opportunities remain conditional on power, planning, construction and customer commitments.

blocks.heading: How much cash does SEGRO really make?

paragraphs.subsection: 5.4 — Debt, its term and property values
paragraphs.text: Debt movements also need decomposition. Euro translation added £166 million to the 2025 net-debt movement without representing new cash borrowing. Operating cash flow was absorbed by development, acquisitions, dividends and financing costs, so net debt cannot be understood from one balance-sheet movement alone.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for SEGRO today?

paragraphs.text: EPRA NTA means EPRA Net Tangible Assets. It estimates what each share represents after valuing SEGRO’s properties, subtracting debt and other obligations, and applying standard property-sector adjustments. It is like estimating the value of a house and investments after paying the mortgage. SEGRO reported EPRA NTA of 902p per share at 30 June 2026, while the share price was 913.20p. That small premium suggests investors value SEGRO’s future earning power above today’s appraised assets.

The UK 10-year government bond yield was 5.38% on 16 October 2026, giving investors a market return against which property must compete. Using 30 June 2026 balances, SEGRO had £5,919 million of net debt, which magnifies both gains and losses. The table brings these judgments together.

dividend.title: SEGRO dividend: payment, cash cover and yield
dividend.meta_description: SEGRO dividend payments, cash coverage, risks and current yield explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: SEGRO's latest full-year dividend is 31.10p per share. SEGRO's operating cash covered the dividend in most of the five years, but fell short by £9 million in 2022 and 2025.
dividend.closing: The full SEGRO memo also explains its business, rivals, management decisions and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does SEGRO pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends distinguish the transaction scenarios. The base and bull cases use £0.2256 in the first period and zero thereafter, because the permitted final dividend is a ceiling and no later SEGRO distributions are forecast after completion. The bear case uses £0.3311 initially, then £0.34 and £0.35, assuming the deal fails or is delayed. The latest full-year dividend was 31.10p, and the payout policy targets 85–95% of adjusted profit after tax. Cash from operations fell £9 million below dividends in 2025, so continued payments are plausible but not risk-free.

blocks.heading: Does SEGRO's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash covered the dividend in most of the five years. It fell short by £9 million in 2022 and 2025. Development and capital spending exceeded £500 million in each year from 2021 through 2024, so property sales, borrowing and share issues also helped fund growth.

paragraphs.text: Development completions added £12 million of potential rent in H1 2026, but only 58 per cent was leased. The development yield was 6.5 per cent. SEGRO also expects 2026 development capital expenditure of £500–550 million, so the pipeline brings future income and a present funding requirement.

Property yields and transaction status are the other decisive signals. A rise in yields or a delayed Prologis completion would increase volatility and compress value. Completion on schedule, alongside sustained rent capture, would support the base or bull interpretation. Management’s longer-term target is about 50p of adjusted EPS by 2030, but delivery against the nearer earnings path matters more.

blocks.heading: What is SEGRO's dividend yield against its share price?

paragraphs.text: Dividend yield is the annual dividend divided by the share price. It can rise because the share price falls, even when the cash dividend is unchanged. Coverage therefore matters more than yield alone.
